reason: Both fully satisfy the hard requirements (snapshot before any risky action, no restart/failover before snapshot, four correctly ordered headings, and abort conditions), but Response B is technically sharper: it correctly notes that restarting the primary only helps if a stuck process (not genuine disk exhaustion) is the cause, proposes resolving a stuck WAL/replication consumer instead of deleting logs outright, adds a load-shedding/throttling mitigation option, and gives more concrete, time-bound abort/rollback conditions (e.g., 'no improvement within 10 minutes, roll back') with explicit escalation paths.
